 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Nov 05, 2026, 14:58:13 IST SUMMARY Nitesh Tiwari’s much-anticipated epic ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’ has finally arrived in cinemas across India and international markets on Thursday, November 5. Starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Goddess Sita and Yash as Ravana, the ambitious adaptation of the Indian epic has generated enormous pre-release buzz, with many describing it as the most expensive film production attempted in the country. 
 Produced by Namit Malhotra, the film has been mounted on an estimated budget of Rs 4,000 crore, with Part 1 costing an estimated Rs 2,000 crore. 
 The film has entered its theatrical run with strong advance-bookings. According to Sacnilk, ‘Ramayana’ recorded Rs 49.75 crore gross in opening-day advance bookings in India, including block seats. Overseas advance sales have reportedly reached approximately USD 5.6 million, taking the combined worldwide advance-booking total beyond Rs 150 crore gross. 
 With such a strong pre-release response, trade estimates suggest that the film could open in the range of Rs 75-100 crore across languages on its first day. Some industry projections have placed its potential lifetime collections between Rs 1,000 crore and Rs 3,000 crore. 
 According to trade tracker Venky Box Office, Prime Focus Studios and Sony Pictures have approved a reported USD 10 million promotional and marketing budget for the film, said to be the highest ever for an Indian production. The report also suggests that the makers are targeting at least USD 65 million in overseas theatrical collections, including USD 30 million from North America. 
 The film is expected to release in multiple languages, catering to audiences across India and overseas. Reports suggest that the Hindi version has a runtime of approximately 3 hours and 15 minutes, while the English version has reportedly been shortened considerably to suit the viewing preferences of international audiences. 
 Early reactions from Indian screenings have been encouraging, with particular attention on Yash's portrayal of Ravana, the film's visual scale and its interpretation of the epic. International viewers have also begun sharing their impressions, with some praising its fantasy elements and comparing its ambition with major Hollywood productions. 
 Stay tuned to the ETimes LIVE blog for the latest updates from theatres, the full movie review, audience reactions, early box-office estimates, occupancy reports, trade analysis, international collections and more as ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’ begins its theatrical journey. Live Events

Amidst the increasing negative opinions about the film, its casting, VFX and music, the actor is hopeful that the film will do wonders. 
 On Tuesday, he took to his X, formerly Twitter, and shared a video of himself talking to the camera. 
 He said, “The ‘Ramayana’ directed by Nitesh Tiwari is being presented to the audience very soon. Many people have said, I too should share my thoughts about this film. Maybe because at one time, I was also a part of the ‘Ramayana’. That time was something else, today the time is something else. I haven't seen the film. Not just for us Indians, but for the entire humanity of the world”. 
 However, he particularly shared that he was disappointed with the film’s music, as it didn’t live up to his expectations despite the collaborations between arguably 2 of the greatest music composers A. R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer. 
 He further mentioned, “There is culture, value, sentiment, emotions, and belief. We all should take care of this heritage. I don't just hope, I have complete faith, Nitesh ji is a very good director. Earlier, he has made very good films. They, and all the artists associated with this film, are very talented. They have come together, worked hard, and made a very good film. In this epic poem, music plays a very important role. In a way, it is the backbone. The music from this film that I have heard, in some of the songs, some of the sounds have disappointed me a bit. I understand that the local flavour, whether it's from Mithla or Ayodhya, should be present in the music behind those songs”. 
 “It should be in the music behind those songs. Although I am not an authority, as a good listener, these are my thoughts. Jai Shri Ram”, he added. 09:06 (IST) Nov 05 'Ramayana' represents our culture, an attempt to raise bar of Indian films: Allu Arjun Telugu superstar Allu Arjun on Wednesday extended his best wishes to the team of "Ramayana", calling the upcoming film an attempt to raise the bar of Indian cinema and a representation of the country's culture.

 "My best wishes to the entire 'Ramayana' team. It's not just a movie. It's a representation of our culture and an attempt to raise the bar of Indian films. I wholeheartedly send my pure, positive wishes to the entire team for their divine attempt," the actor wrote on his Instagram Stories. 
 "Let's all unite and come forward to support a pure attempt that carries our stories, our culture and our glory. Jai Sri Ram," he added. 09:00 (IST) Nov 05 'Ramayana' advance booking day 1 crosses Rs 50 crore mark ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’ has strengthened its opening-day prospects, with advance bookings crossing the Rs 50 crore mark in India. According to the latest Sacnilk update, Nitesh Tiwari’s epic has recorded Rs 50.08 crore gross in Day 1 advance sales, including block seats, while collections stand at Rs 42.96 crore without block seats. The film has sold 14.05 lakh tickets (12.14 lakh excluding block seats) across 26,615 shows for Thursday, November 5. The latest figures mark an increase from its earlier advance-booking tally of Rs 49.75 crore gross. 08:58 (IST) Nov 05 ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’ Twitter reviews: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash starrer gets mixed reactions; Ravana hailed as ‘scene stealer’, VFX praised but story faces criticism Director Nitesh Tiwari and producer Namit Malhotra's much-anticipated epic ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash, has finally arrived in cinemas, and the first reactions from moviegoers have begun pouring in on social media. 
 While the film has generated considerable excitement for its ambitious scale, visual effects, Rs 4,000 crore budget and star-studded cast, early audience reactions appear divided, with viewers praising the visual elements, while others were critical of the storytelling. 
 With screening starting as early as 6.30 am on Thursday morning, fans took to their Twitter handles to share early reviews, while trying to leave out spoilers. One thing for sure, audiences have left the theatres singing praise of Yash’s menacing portrayal of Ravana, which emerged as one of the biggest talking points among viewers. 
 Yash is being hailed as a ‘scene stealer’, with his 'aura', screen presence and performance drawing considerable attention away from the leading cast. However, many have also praised Ranbir Kapoor for his work in bringing Lord Rama to life on the big screen. 
 The film's visual effects, production design and grand cinematic presentation, had audiences going gaga, appreciating the scale at which the epic has been brought to the big screen. 07:23 (IST) Nov 05 Ranbir Kapoor, Yash starrer Ramayana declared tax free in West Bengal West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that the upcoming Bollywood movie Ramayana, starring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash, will be made tax-free in the state. He announced this as the cast joined him in Dussehra celebrations in Kolkata. 
 Announcing the tax exemption, Adhikari said that ‘Ramayana’ would join other films that have received tax-free status in the state. He also spoke about the possibility of films based on other Indian epics and mythological figures. 
 “‘The Ramayana’ film has been made tax-free. ‘The Kerala Story’, ‘The Kashmir Files’ and ‘The Bengal Files’, all of these will be or have been made tax-free, and the same will apply to ‘Ramayana’. In the days to come, we will see films on Shri Krishna and Arjuna, as well as the Mahabharata,” the West bengal CM told ANI. 
 Ranbir, who plays Lord Ram in the epic, thanked the CM and the people present for welcoming the film's team to Kolkata for the festival. 
 “It is a matter of great happiness and good fortune for us to come to this sacred land of Kolkata and celebrate Dussehra with all of you,” Ranbir said. 07:08 (IST) Nov 05 Rakul Preet Singh reveals what made give her nod to portray Surpanakha in ‘Ramayana’ Actress Rakul Preet Singh, who is awaiting the release of her upcoming epic film ‘Ramayana’, has shared insights into her role of Surpanakha in the film. 
 The actress, who essays the role of Ravana’s sister, has revealed what drew her to the character and the opportunity to explore a side of Surpanakha that goes beyond the conventional portrayal of her as an antagonist. 
 Talking about her part in the film, the actress said, “Every few years, you see a different interpretation and presentation of these characters, while keeping the essence rooted in the original text. As an actor, you only look at a character from that lens, that it's a character that has layers, that has the possibility and ability to shine through the film. She was apparently the most beautiful woman of Lanka. She had an ego, but then she was layered. As an actor, it's fun to explore those layers”. 07:07 (IST) Nov 05 Yash says ‘Ramayana’ goes beyond one film industry; calls for unity in Indian cinema Actor Yash has emphasized that the upcoming epic film ‘Ramayana’ goes beyond the boundaries of any one film industry. 
 He called for the entire Indian film fraternity to come together to take the country’s stories, culture, and history to a global audience. Speaking at the film's promotional event, Yash said, “This Ramayana is in all our blood. So, when making this film, this is not a work that can happen from just any one film industry. The entire Indian film industry must come together.” 
 Talking about the need to take Indian stories beyond geographical boundaries, Yash stressed that the country must take pride in its culture and history. “What is our history? What is our culture? If we sit waiting for someone else to say it, it cannot be told.” 06:33 (IST) Nov 05 Namit Malhotra lauds Ranbir Kapoor's performance in 'Ramayana': "Finest actor of our generation" Producer Namit Malhotra reflected on his professional and personal bond with Ranbir Kapoor, recalling the time when they used to share meals to finally collaborating for the film 'Ramayana'. 
 Taking to his X handle, Namit praised Ranbir's "resilience" and talent while expressing his confidence in the actor's performance as Lord Rama in the upcoming film. 
 Namot Malhotra wrote, "From watching our fathers share meals and laughter to now, four decades later, coming together to tell one of the greatest epics of all time. It's been quite a journey. I have witnessed your journey closely. The highs, the setbacks, the quiet resilience, and the way you've stayed so grounded through it all, both on and off screen. There was never a doubt in my mind. There is no one better to portray Lord Rama." 
 "You are, without doubt, the finest actor of our generation. Being named among @TIME's 100 Most Influential People of 2026 feels absolutely deserving. It's great to see the world finally take notice of you and your talent. This is just the beginning, my friend. More power to you," concluded Namit Malhotra. 06:26 (IST) Nov 05 Rakul Preet Singh calls ‘Ramayana’ a larger-than-life experience: ‘We represent Bharat to the world’ Actress Rakul Preet Singh has expressed her excitement and pride about being part of the much-anticipated epic ‘Ramayana.’ 
 She called the project a journey that goes beyond cinema. In her recent post on Instagram, the actress shared that being associated with a story rooted in India’s history, heritage, and culture is an honour and a truly unforgettable experience. Rakul shared glimpses from the grand trailer launch event of Ramayana and opened up about being a part of the epic project. 
 Sharing pictures from the special occasion, the ‘Runway 34’ actress wrote, “An honour to be a part of something that feels larger than life, larger than cinema, our history, our heritage, our Ramayana. We represent Bharat to the world, a feeling that’s truly beyond words. Can’t wait for you all to step into this world with us.” 
 Rakul Preet Singh will be seen portraying Surpanakha, the powerful and fierce sister of demon king Ravana, in Nitesh Tiwari’s upcoming two-part epic. 06:22 (IST) Nov 05 SS Rajamouli cheers for team 'Ramayana' ahead of November 5 release Renowned filmmaker SS Rajamouli has extended his support for Nitesh Tiwari's highly anticipated mythological drama 'Ramayana Part 1' ahead of its theatrical release on November 5 this year. 
 The 'Baahubali' maker used social media to pen a note of appreciation for the cast and crew for bringing the mythological tale alive on screen. Rajamouli stated that it was exciting for him to witness an Indian movie being made on such a massive scale. He also went on to congratulate the 'Ramayana' team for bringing the characters to life with such depth. 
 Taking to his X (Formerly known as Twitter) timeline, Rajamouli stated, "#Ramayana is a story every Indian storyteller grows up aspiring to tell. It's a joy to see @niteshtiwari22 and @malhotra_namit bring it to the screen on such a grand scale. Each actor brings these timeless characters to life with depth. Looking forward to 5th November. Best wishes to the entire team. (sic)." 
 Previously, during his appearance on the Empire Film Podcast, Rajamouli shared his views on cinematic adaptations of the epic tales of 'Ramayana' and 'Mahabharata'. He admitted that he was never completely happy with the depiction of the tales on the screen. 
 “I was never fully satisfied with how these epics were presented on screen,” the 'RRR' maker shared. 06:12 (IST) Nov 05 Yash explains his unusual trick of getting into headspace of his character of Lankesh in ‘Ramayana’ ctor Yash, who is gearing up for the release of his upcoming epic ‘Ramayana’, has shared that he used to play songs of Lord Shiva on full volume while shooting for the film. 
 The team of ‘Ramayana’ graced the ongoing edition of the San Diego Comic-Con 2026 recently, where they spoke about the film. During the event, Yash, who essays the role of Lankesh in the film, shared that in order to become one with the character, he used music as a vehicle to get into the mindspace of the character as Ravana was a devotee of Lord Shiva. 
 Sharing his experience of working on the film, Yash told ‘Review Nation’, “I kind of spoiled the whole atmosphere of the set. I used to be very serious. I used to get big speakers and just play music at full volume. So, I used to be in that zone. I used to play Shiva songs”. 
 “Ravana is a big devotee of Lord Shiva. I used to play that and I wanted to be in that trance. Forcefully, all of them would talk with a lot of difficulty because the music used to be so loud”, he added. 06:11 (IST) Nov 05 Sunny Deol confirms he has done little work on ‘Ramayana’ ctor Sunny Deol, who will be seen essaying the role of Lord Hanuman in the upcoming epic ‘Ramayana’, has said that he had a very limited scope of work in whatever he has shot for in the upcoming film.
